title: River Development Agent Production Governed Operation Execution Authorization Consumption Integration
objective: Connect deterministic production acquisition of the existing governed operation-execution authorization to the existing operational executor integration entry boundary at real production execution call sites, while preserving default-deny behavior and without creating, upgrading, or broadening authorization.

includes: Consume the DEV-317 governed operation-execution authorization acquisition integration from production execution paths that currently enter DEV-314 without supplied governed authorization.
Pass only the acquired existing governed authorization into the DEV-314 operational executor integration entry boundary.
Preserve DEV-314 as the authoritative admission boundary for apply-mode execution.
Preserve dry-run behavior as non-mutating and independent of mutation authorization.
Preserve default-deny behavior when governed authorization is absent, untrusted, not ready, unauthorized, malformed, or otherwise unusable.
Integrate production authorization consumption without creating new authorization authority.
Add deterministic tests proving authorized production consumption and unauthorized/default-deny behavior.
Keep the integration narrowly scoped to authorization acquisition-to-consumption wiring.
excludes: Upgrading, expanding, synthesizing, or repairing authorization.
Treating --apply or requested apply mode as authorization.
Bypassing the DEV-314 operational executor integration entry boundary.
Changing the underlying governed authorization decision semantics established by DEV-307.
Changing the inert authorization acquisition semantics established by DEV-317.
Adding retry, persistence, push, deployment, secret-access, network, or external-side-effect authority.
Broad refactoring unrelated to the production authorization-consumption seam.

invariants: DEV-317 acquisition remains deterministic and does not itself execute repository operations.
DEV-314 remains the authoritative operational admission boundary.
Requested apply mode is never authorization.
Missing governed authorization remains denied for apply-mode execution.
Only a valid existing governed OPERATION_EXECUTION_AUTHORIZED result may satisfy governed apply authorization.
No authorization is created, upgraded, broadened, synthesized, or inferred by DEV-318.
No new repository mutation primitive is introduced.
Existing safety, policy, path, and execution-runner boundaries remain intact.
acceptanceCriteria: At least one real production execution path consumes DEV-317 acquisition rather than leaving DEV-317 with zero production consumers.
The acquired governed authorization is supplied to the existing DEV-314 operational entry boundary.
Authorized apply-mode execution can reach the existing runner only after DEV-314 admission.
Apply-mode execution remains blocked when governed authorization cannot be acquired or does not satisfy DEV-314.
Dry-run remains operational without mutation authorization and remains non-mutating.
Tests prove both authorized and denied production consumption paths.
No caller can convert --apply alone into governed authorization.
Full River Dev baseline tests pass.
implementationNotes: Prefer a narrow integration adapter over embedding authorization-acquisition logic directly into package-executor.ts, implement.ts, or index.ts.
The implementation must consume DEV-317 output and produce only the authorization input required by the existing DEV-314 boundary.
Do not duplicate DEV-307 authorization logic.
Do not duplicate DEV-314 admission logic.
Do not make the consumption adapter itself mutation-capable.
Before implementation, inspect the exact DEV-317 exported function signature and its dependency requirements and determine the smallest production caller integration point.
